# WPF Gotchas

> Known WPF (Windows Presentation Foundation / XAML) patterns that cause silent failures or hard-to-debug errors.

## Entries

- [TemplateBinding does no type conversion; StringFormat ignored on object targets](templatebinding-no-conversion.md): A templated control bound to a non-string value renders empty with no binding error; Binding.StringFormat only works on string-typed targets. Use ContentPresenter + ContentStringFormat. HIGH.
- [Topmost=True can silently lose its Win32 z-band](topmost-lost-on-activation.md): A non-activated transparent topmost overlay drops behind normal windows when the same app activates another window; window.Topmost still reads True. Re-assert with SetWindowPos(HWND_TOPMOST, SWP_NOACTIVATE). HIGH.
- [SizeToContent window positioned after Show() lands at default cascade spot on first show](sizetocontent-position-after-show.md): Final size settles after Show() (layout + per-monitor DPI pass), so Left/Top set right after Show() use a stale size; first show only, later shows work. Pre-position before Show and re-anchor in SizeChanged. HIGH.
- [DispatcherTimer capped near 64 Hz by default ~15.6 ms Windows timer resolution](dispatchertimer-64hz-timer-resolution.md): Intervals below ~15.6 ms are silently quantized, so a 144/240 fps loop runs at ~64 fps; call winmm timeBeginPeriod(1) when needed and timeEndPeriod(1) when done (system-wide power drain). Sub-lesson: rescale per-tick easing/decay coefficients to the actual tick length (1 - Math.Pow(base, intervalMs/refMs)) or animation speed changes with frame rate. MEDIUM.
